The recent series of actions have been focused on verifying and fixing UI behavior in the Teich Studio web interface. I started by launching the studio server on a temporary directory, confirmed it was up, and then used the preview tools to open a debugging session. I navigated to the "prompts" view, added a new prompt, saved it, and then observed that optional fields were still visible despite being marked as hidden. I identified the cause as CSS rules that set `display: grid` or `flex` on certain classes, which override the HTML `hidden` attribute. To address this globally, I edited `src/teich/studio/static/style.css`, adding a rule for `[hidden] { display: none !important; }` right after the existing universal selector. After applying that change, I reloaded the page to see the effect.

Now that the CSS fix is in place, I need to verify that the hidden fields are indeed hidden across the different parts of the UI. The studio UI has multiple main views accessible via the navigation bar: "prompts", "interactive", "chat", etc. I've already inspected the "prompts" view; the next logical step is to check the "interactive" view, which also contains optional input fields that could be affected by the hidden attribute. By clicking the navigation item for the interactive view (`.nav-item[data-view="interactive"]`), I can load that view and then perform further checks (e.g., inspecting hidden fields, possibly adding a test interaction) to confirm the CSS rule works universally.

Thus, the immediate next action is to simulate a click on the navigation element that switches to the interactive view. This aligns with the pattern of using `mcp__Claude_Preview__preview_click` to interact with the UI, and the selector `.nav-item[data-view="interactive"]` precisely targets the interactive tab. Executing this click will load the interactive view, allowing me to continue the verification process.

Proceed with the click on the interactive view navigation item.
